Finding.Text: The end revision 6787800 carries the line "Change: C-0013-verified-change-commits" as the third line of a prose paragraph, and git 2.53.0.windows.2 parses no trailer from that message: both "git interpret-trailers --parse" and "%(trailers:key=Change,valueonly)" return empty on it. The routine constructs the trailer as its own final paragraph via a second -m, a shape that always parses (the CK2 tests assert the parsed value), so this commit is not the routine's verified output and the change's own product commit has no mechanically readable attribution. That is the P-016 failure class the Problem cites; D2 rules that a trailer mentioned only in prose does not count; and the grace5-execute instruction landed in this same commit requires the routine for every change-owned product commit. Repair is constrained: N2 and K3 forbid automatic rewrite of referenced history, and amending 6787800 would orphan the source-revision run-2 names and this review's end-revision, so any repair is a separate owner-visible operation (D4) followed by fresh final evidence and review, or an explicit owner disposition.

The tool's git() helper runs git without -c core.quotepath=false and the path read-back parses "git show --pretty=format: --name-only HEAD" line-wise, while the kernel's own git helpers (src/git.ts and src/upgrade/kernel-source.ts) disable quotepath and use -z for path lists. Under git's default core.quotepath=true a supplied path containing non-ASCII characters, a double quote or a backslash is printed quoted with octal escapes; normalisePath converts the escape backslashes to slashes, so the committed-path comparison mismatches and the tool exits 1 with "committed path set differs" after creating a correct commit. The failure is reported and the commit stays visible, but a valid owned path is falsely refused and the next handoff stops on a spurious mismatch. Align the git calls with src/git.ts: pass -c core.quotepath=false and read the name list with -z.

The run-2 log shows the command and exit 0. A pass discriminates A7's type-check obligation from a broken build.
